newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia 97 PGM exports to Japan seen a little lower.
newsitem.headline: Russia 97 PGM exports to Japan seen a little lower.

text.p: Russia's 1997 exports of platinum group metals to Japan will be a little below 1996 levels, a precious metals official at the Finance Ministry said on Friday.

"The levels will be a little bit less than they were in 1996," Vladimir Rybkin, head of the ministry's precious metals and stones department, told Reuters by telephone. He declined to give concrete numbers or say by how much exports would decline.

Rybkin said levels had been set by the government before officials from Almazjuvelirexport, the state precious metals export agency, travelled to Tokyo, where they are now, for long-delayed contract talks.
But he added, "Everything can change by the end of the year.

"There are a number of factors -- the market, our hard currency needs. If we need hard currency, we may increase the volumes. If we don't need hard currency, then we won't." He gave no further details.
Almazjuvelirexport officials told Reuters in Tokyo on Friday that supplies could resume this month but it was too early to comment on volumes.

Japan is the world's largest consumer of PGMs. Russia is the world's top supplier of palladium and the second-largest of platinum. Both metals are at highs over worries about delays in Russian supplies and diminishing Russian stockpiles.
